**1 — Scene:** A cooked breakfast-style meal of scrambled eggs, roasted potatoes, and Brussels sprouts.

**2 — Vessel:** A square dinner plate, partly cropped. I estimate its usable area as roughly equivalent to a **26 cm round plate**: 3.14 × 13² ≈ **530 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Scrambled eggs, skin-on potato chunks, Brussels sprouts, and a light sheen of cooking fat. No distinct sauce is visible.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrambled eggs | 27% | 143 cm² × 1.5 cm = 215 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 193 g | 145 | 280 kcal |
| Roasted potatoes | 24% | 127 cm² × 2 cm = 254 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 153 g | 95 | 145 kcal |
| Brussels sprouts | 14% | 74 cm² × 2.2 cm = 163 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 98 g | 40 | 39 kcal |
| Cooking fat | Thin coating* | Approximately 8 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 7 g | 880 | 62 kcal |

The food footprints total **65% of the plate**. *The fat coats those foods rather than covering additional plate area; its quantity is especially uncertain. Food energy values exclude this separately counted fat.*

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **451 g and 526 kcal** is plausible for the visible substantial egg portion, potato chunks, and small pile of sprouts. Plate size, pile height, and cooking fat are the largest uncertainties.
